title: The Fleet — overview
note: A simplified, opaque view of the fleet. The operator makes the judgment calls and wraps them in a toolkit of /fleet-* skills — the intelligent layer over the mechanical fleetc CLI — which (with the operator's own raw verbs) actuate fleetc; fleetc drives fleetd (the daemon, shown as one box — no internal state machines); fleetd actuates its external systems (a Tracker, a Forge), persists to the Ledger, works inside a Project (the worktrees), and spawns the Crew of cogs. For what fleetd persists (the domain types and every ledger table) switch to the Data model.

detail.summary: Grills the operator on what fleet.toml needs (forge, tracker, checkout, merge policy), then creates projects/<name>/ with its fleet.toml, tickets/, review/ and impl/ folders and its checkout, and runs preflight until it's green.

Reads the product's merged design canon (design records, specs, conventions, Definition of Ready/Done on origin/HEAD) and the code they point to, before a mission that needs the whole design. The admiral's, on a grooming session.

Drafts a new ticket to /fleet-ready-done (title, four-section body, duplicate check, blockers + convoy, Ready check), then creates it with `fleetc ticket new` on whichever tracker the project uses. For the admiral and the operator: files work, never dispatches it.

detail.type: skill · groom a convoy to Ready
detail.summary: Grooms a whole convoy as one: each ticket meets the Definition of Ready, together they cover the plan's outcome, every blocker edge is needed and none is missing, and the critical path is never held up by deferrable work. Reports first, applies what the operator approves. For the admiral.

detail.type: skill · the Definition of Ready and Done
detail.summary: The fleet's reference for how a ticket is structured, when it is Ready to dispatch, and when an MR meets Done. /fleet-commission and /fleet-propose draft to it; the captain judges Ready against it, the worker and the reviewer Done. A project's own stricter doctrine extends it.

Settles the open proposals, re-judges the anchored tickets, keeps every ticket in the convoy it belongs to, and checks the fleet's pace against its deadlines and its machinery's health. One numbered action each with its fleetc command; acts only on the operator's OK. For the shipwright.

One self-contained HTML page: the convoy's and its critical path's % grade, a board of its tickets by column (the critical path in red), the proposals waiting to join it, its plan, and each ticket linked to the tracker. Read-only. For the shipwright.

One self-contained HTML dashboard from the telemetry: the total, the last 24 h and 7 days, the cost per Done ticket, the cache hit rate, and USD by day, role, convoy, ticket and model. Read-only. For the shipwright.

detail.type: skill · ship the viewer to Splash
detail.summary: Builds the demos/architecture viewer into a single self-contained HTML file and publishes it to a Splash page at a stable, SSO-gated URL (Okta handled via a vendored Chrome extension — no token or persisted cookie). First run creates the page and returns its URL; later runs replace the same page.

Creates a git worktree + branch for a ticket in its project's impl/ folder, forked off a given base (default: origin's default branch). Pure worktree creation — no ticket lifecycle. Run when producing a dispatch, then pass the path to `fleetc dispatch --worktree`; reconcile spawns the cog there (reconcile never creates worktrees).

Dispatches the lookout to weigh a cog's escalation against its transcript, worktree, ticket and convoy plan, and return a verdict: REFUTE (a way out keeps the ticket's intent, fits the plan and clears the blocker — sent to the cog) or CONFIRM (the operator rules). For the admiral and captains.

Launches the current branch's ship: pushes it, drafts the MR title + description from the ticket and the branch's divergence from its base, then opens the MR via `fleetc launch` (fleetd's forge adapter opens it — GitLab or GitHub alike). Run from the worktree.

Reviews one MR, ours or an ally's, against its ticket, Done and the project's own doctrine, and posts the findings — on ours a resolvable thread each, on an ally's one summary comment. Returns VERDICT: clean | changes; never approves. The lookout's default (a project names its own: review_skill).

Answers the open review threads on the ticket's MR through `fleetc review` / `fleetc reply` (forge-neutral): proves each finding against the code before fixing it, proposes it or pushes back with evidence, defers nits to one follow-up. Count-gated; surfaces floating notes before declaring the MR clean.

Rebases the ticket's MR against its target. Clean divergence → triggers the forge's server-side rebase via `fleetc rebase` and exits (the sailor re-fires on the result). Conflict → resolves locally with project/code understanding and force-pushes. Escalates only when the conflict needs a product/design decision.

detail.type: skill · fix a broken CI run
detail.summary: Classifies a broken CI run on the ticket's MR (read through `fleetc ci`, forge-neutral) and attempts a good-faith fix (retry / lint / build / test / config); escalates if it's unclassifiable or out of scope.

Drafts work a cog found that isn't its own — a bug nearby, debt, a reviewer's out-of-scope ask, an existing ticket to take on — and proposes it with `fleetc propose`: filed at once, labelled fleet-proposed and outside any convoy, for the operator (or the admiral) to accept or drop. For a worker, sailor or hand.

The operator's "pawn it off" handoff: yields a hand's work to a sailor. Reports `concluded` via fleetc, so fleetd promotes the order to auto, moves the ticket → In QA, requests review, and reaps the hand. A ticketless hand has no sailor to yield to. Run from the hand's worktree.
On the Overview fleetd is one opaque box. Inside, its heart is a single scheduling loop (scheduler.rs::run) — the state machine below.

stateMachine.note: Verified against scheduler.rs::run. Each pass fires any ticker whose Instant deadline has passed, then blocks on the mpsc command channel for ≤500ms (Timeout → re-loop). poll is READ-ONLY (overwrites the in-memory liveness snapshot — no ledger write, no event); sync, live reconcile, and each client command are the single writer's writes — one transaction appending a CDC event. Each sync is followed by the health check on the project's git state and its guards: a miss holds the lookouts (and is logged as health_checked when it changes). A Disconnected channel (UDS server gone) breaks the loop. Cadences shown are the config defaults (5/300/60s), re-read live each pass.

detail.type: a crew cog · Claude session in a tmux pane
detail.summary: One pass over one convoy, on a timer (captain_sleep_secs): dispatches its clean frontier, inspects its cogs' escalations, closes it once every ticket is delivered.

detail.type: a crew cog · Claude session in a tmux pane
detail.summary: Implements one ticket in one worktree to a draft MR, answers its review round after round until a review comes back clean, then concludes.

detail.type: a crew cog · Claude session in a tmux pane
detail.summary: Operator-driven implementer — you write the code; it grounds the ticket, aids on request, and concludes when you say so.

detail.type: a crew cog · Claude session in a tmux pane
detail.summary: Lands one open MR: one finishing sweep (rebase / reply / CI fix / arm), then sleeps until the ship needs it again.

detail.type: a crew cog · Claude session in a tmux pane
detail.summary: Reviews one MR — ours or an ally's — in its own review worktree (review/<iid>), posts, and stands down. One per MR, several at once.

detail.type: a crew cog · Claude session in a tmux pane
detail.summary: Convened by fleetd on a ticket's confirmed escalation, for the operator to rule with (capped by `admirals`). Reports no states.

Read once at launch. [forge] + [tracker] are required; everything else defaults. The cadences, caps, review levers, thresholds and dry_run are live: `fleetc settings set` overrides them with no restart.

rows.informs: Liveness-poll cadence (s): how often the in-memory cog snapshot refreshes.
Sync cadence (s): hydrate the ledger from the tracker + forge.
Reconcile cadence (s): converge intent against reality.
A convoy's rest (s) between captain passes, from the last one's finish.
true = plan + log only, execute nothing (the parity look).
Admirals convened at once, one per confirmed escalation (-1 = no cap, 0 = none).
Lookouts reviewing allied MRs at once, one MR each (-1 = no cap, 0 = none).
Lookouts reviewing our own MRs at once, apart from the allies' cap.
Review rounds a worker gets on its MR; past them with threads open, it escalates.
How long an MR's threads must hold still before a sailor answers them (0 = at once).
The project's own review skill, which every lookout runs (unset = /fleet-review).
The project's grooming skill, run by an admiral on each ticket it grooms (unset = /fleet-ready-done).
The project's read-only readiness check, before dispatch and at grooming (unset = /fleet-ready-done).
Activity age under which a cog counts as Active.
Age under which a cog is Quiet; beyond it → Idle / Dead.
Bind addr of the OTLP/HTTP receiver that fills telemetry.db.
Product's main checkout (relative to fleet.toml): owns the impl/ ticket worktrees and the lookouts' review/ worktrees; captains launch here.
Which forge adapter drives the MRs.
GitLab numeric project id, or GitHub owner/repo.
true = `fleetc arm` sets the MR to merge once its gates pass; false = arm refuses, the operator merges on the forge.
Which tracker adapter holds tickets.
Tracker project; for Jira also the ticket-key prefix (PROJ → PROJ-12).
Label a worker's claim adds to the ticket.
Filesystem tracker: folder of ticket files.
Filesystem tracker: who "me" is for a claim.
